title_en: Opinion of the Supreme People's Court on How to Handle Original Commutation Rulings When a Criminal Is Subject to Combined Punishment for Multiple Crimes Due to Omitted Crimes or New Crimes
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinion on How to Handle the Original Commutation Ruling When Combining Punishments for Omitted Crimes or New Crimes

Fa [2012] No. 44

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Recently, this Court has received requests from some local higher people's courts regarding how to handle the original commutation ruling when, after the pronouncement of judgment but before the completion of the sentence, a criminal is subject to merger of punishments for having committed an omitted crime or a new crime. To unify the application of law, upon deliberation, the following opinion is hereby put forward:

After a criminal has been granted a commutation by ruling, when a merger of punishments is conducted according to law due to the discovery of an omitted crime or the commission of a new crime, the term of sentence reduced by the commutation ruling shall not be counted as part of the sentence already served.

Thereafter, when granting commutation according to law to a criminal subject to merger of punishments for an omitted crime, and when determining the frequency and extent of commutation, the term of sentence previously reduced by the commutation ruling shall be taken into appropriate consideration.

January 18, 2012
